question: Why is the Northern Sparsely Populated Areas (NSPA) network not included in the Commission’s proposal for a regulation on national and regional partnership plans?

How will the Commission ensure that, in the forthcoming 2028-2034 financial period, the specific NSPA funding enshrined in the Accession Treaties of Finland and Sweden will remain a separate, ring-fenced funding component under EU primary law, with clear and quantitative allocation criteria guaranteeing at least the current level of funding?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.1.

2026) While the Commission proposal1 does not prescibe which partners in Members States should be involved in preparing and implementing the national and regional partnership plans - thus respecting the institutional, legal and administrative arrangements of each Member State, Article 21(2) of the proposal sets out that each Member State shall prepare and implement the plan in partnership with partners, including regional and local authorities.

Article 6 of the proposal also requires to organise and implement a comprehensive partnership taking into account the specificities of the chapters concerned and that partnership must include a balanced representation of relevant partners.

The next EU budget will continue to provide strong support to northern sparsely populated regions, taking into account their specific needs and challenges such as natural or demographic handicaps, especially regarding connectivity and accessibility. Member States are obliged to indicate in the plans the total estimated costs of such support, including the EU contribution2.

Further, Annex VII of the proposal sets out that Member States shall allocate resources to tackling economic, social and territorial disparities taking into account specific needs and challenges of Northern Sparsely Populated Areas. The corresponding allocation can be programmed by the Member State within the flexibility embedded in the proposal.
Furthermore, the Commission3 suggested to consider specific safeguards to ensure continuity in transition and more developed regions.
